reason: Reporting matches an early-morning arrival (about four hours before) and an 11:51 a.m. campus entry, but Hull testified Robinson was seen on surveillance returning to UVU just after 10 a.m., which conflicts with the four hours being unaccounted for.
Prosecutors allege Robinson confessed in messages and a note to Twiggs, which conflicts with the host's statement that 'they' acknowledge he never confessed.
Authorities and Kash Patel said Robinson's father recognized him and convinced him to turn himself in, which sits in tension with the host's report that the parents do not believe he did it.
David Hull testified the SBI collected and verified doorbell camera footage from a residence near UVU, contrary to the host's assertion that it could not be doorbell footage.
Hull testified surveillance shows the man walking with a limp, his right leg not bending, which conflicts with the host's inference that both legs bend.
A Twiggs relative told Fox News he was kicked out at age 18, not in junior year of high school as the host relays.

Sheriff Nate Brooksby is quoted saying the retired detective who arranged the surrender was not the family's bishop or another church leader, which is in tension with the host's report that the detective is an LDS Boy Scout leader; the reporting does not name the detective, so this goes to open questions rather than a dispute.

Prosecutors call the evidence against Robinson overwhelming and KSL reports messages in which Robinson claimed he shot Kirk, which conflicts with the host's theory; this is opinion against reporting, not a two-source dispute.

Harpole is reported saying his team was denied permission to fly drones under FAA and campus rules, which conflicts with the host's conclusion that the team had drones sending footage; this is the subject's own account, not an independent dispute.

Court-presented surveillance video and investigators place Tyler Robinson on the UVU campus on Sept. 10, conflicting with the host's belief he was not on campus; reporting says the host is wrong rather than two sources disputing, so it goes to open questions.

Reporting says prosecutors cite a 'mountain of evidence' and presented much of it at a five-day hearing, and that statements are characterised as a confession, conflicting with the host's assertion that there is no evidence beyond messages and no confession.
The host's belief is opinion, but reporting conflicts with it: the Kirk family cites 'overwhelming evidence' and officials say Robinson told investigators he killed Kirk.

TPUSA COO Justin Streiff told the Deseret News that new chapter requests rose to around 50,000 after the assassination, against the 100,000 figure the host attributes to Erika Kirk on the call; this conflicts on the number, not on whether she said it.
Reporting dates TPUSA's announcement of Erika Kirk as CEO and board chair to Thursday, Sept. 18, 2025, not the day after a Sept. 16 call as the host says.
Reporting dates the TPUSA announcement naming Erika Kirk CEO and chair to Thursday, Sept. 18, 2025, not Sept. 17; Doug DeGroote's sign-off is not addressed.

TPUSA COO Justin Streiff told the Deseret News that last year's donations, the group's biggest ever, exceeded $115 million, which is hard to square with the host's claim of $250 million in a couple of months; this is reporting against the host, not two sources in conflict.

Authorities and Kash Patel are reported as saying Robinson's father recognized his son from the released images and got him to turn himself in, which cuts against the host's claim; this is reporting against the host, not a dispute between two sources.
FBI analyst Amanda Bakker testified she attributed all of the DNA to two people after rerunning tests, which conflicts with the host's claim of five other sets of DNA on the rifle.

AP reports prosecutors planned to present Washington County Sheriff's Office video from Sept. 11 when Robinson turned himself in, and an agent narrated such a clip in court, which conflicts with the claim that the arrival tape is lost.
Deseret News reported Erika Kirk gave a live video statement two days after the murder that she had written, conflicting with the host's sourced claim that Blake Neff wrote it.
JD Vance said Erika Kirk skipped the Georgia event because she received threats, conflicting with the host's assertion that crowd size was the real reason.

The TPUSA board said Charlie Kirk had expressed that he wanted his wife to take over if he died, which conflicts with the donors' account the host relays, so this is an open question rather than a dispute.

Agent Brian Davis told the court Lance Twiggs' recorded April 20 interview was used in lieu of bringing him to the preliminary hearing as a witness, contrary to the host's expectation that Twiggs would testify.
In the CBS town hall with Bari Weiss, Erika Kirk is reported saying Charlie called 'Jew hate' brain rot, not that anyone who does not support Israel has brain rot.
Erika Kirk's reported 'brain rot' remark was that Charlie said 'Jew hate was brain rot', not that people asking questions about Israel have brain rot.
Erika Kirk's reported 'brain rot' remark referred to 'Jew hate', not to opposition to Israel; the rest of the claim is characterisation not covered.

Host's belief that Robinson did not kill Kirk and was set up by Twiggs conflicts with KSL's report that Twiggs confirmed what Robinson told him about the crime and court documents quoting Robinson's 'I am, I'm sorry' reply; this is theory, so it is not disputed.

Host's denial that Robinson fired from the Losee Center roof conflicts with prosecutors' allegation and reported footage of a person going prone on that roof; it is the host's belief against allegations, so it goes to open questions.

Host calls the parents-turned-him-in story a lie, but charging documents say his mother recognized him and his parents confronted him, and Nate Brooksby says the parents helped negotiate his surrender.
Host says Robinson was not political, but his mother told investigators he had become more political and leaned left, and prosecutors say he targeted Kirk for his political expression.
The witness's statement that the figure was not on the roof at 12:15 conflicts with Agent Hull's testimony that investigators believe Robinson got onto the Losee roof at about 12:15 p.m.
Fox News reports the jury awarded nearly $1 billion to the Sandy Hook families, not the $1.4 billion the host states (the difference may reflect later punitive damages).
Reporting states Robinson turned himself in, that a video of it was narrated in testimony, and Patel says his father turned him in, contrary to the host's claim none of this was shown.
Fox News reports the autopsy testimony ruled out exploding-microphone theories, and prosecutors allege the shot came from the Losee Center roof, against the host's view.

Fox News, citing a law enforcement source, describes Lance Twiggs as Robinson's transgender partner, and Kash Patel said Robinson's father turned him in, which conflicts with the host calling those claims lies.
Sheriff Brooksby said Robinson had 'suicidal ideations', which conflicts with the host calling that a lie, though Brooksby's account supports her point that Robinson agreed to surrender peacefully.
Harpole's account as reported says Rick Cutler held onto Harpole's shirt to keep Harpole from falling out of the van, not that Cutler was holding Charlie because his feet were hanging out.

Testimony and prosecution evidence place Robinson arriving by car in the campus garage at about 8:30 a.m., which conflicts with the host's inference that he was already parked off campus; the TMZ 8:07 footage itself is not addressed.
Investigator testimony and the court video compilation show the suspect returning in a long-sleeved black shirt, which conflicts with the host's belief that he never changed into it.

The host says Zacharia now acknowledges she is not an attorney, but the Deseret News identifies her as "attorney Katie Zacharia" in quoting her Fox and Friends remarks; this is reporting at odds with the claim, not two sources disputing it, so it goes to the open-questions register.
